To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the risk of local recurrence of giant cell tumor of bone (GCTB) after curettage is high and that the risk is increased with the number of recurrences, the presence of an intralesional fracture, and a history of previous surgery.

the risk of local recurrence after treatment of a primary GCT is associated with the presence of an intracortical extension of the tumor, a high histologic grade of tumor necrosis, and the presence of a soft tissue mass.

the following nonsurgical factors are associated with local recurrence of giant cell tumors of bone (GCTB): (1) incomplete resection of the tumor, (2) presence of a soft-tissue component, (3) tumor size > 8 cm, (4) location of the tumor in the pelvis, (5) presence of neurovascular involvement, (6) tumor recurrence at a different site, and (7) presence of metastases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of factors associated with local recurrences of giant cell tumors of bone.
the identification of factors associated with local tumor recurrence in patients with giant cell tumor of bone.
the development of a new class of drugs that are designed to be effective against a broad range of tumors, while minimizing side effects on the patient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most important factors associated with local tumor recurrence are tumor size, tumor location, and the presence or absence of an associated pseudocyst.
the most important factors associated with local control in GCT of bone are tumor size, location, and surgical margin.
the most important factor associated with local recurrence is the extent of surgical resection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of this study are in keeping with the current literature and support the use of a multidisciplinary approach in the treatment of giant cell tumors.
the results of the present study suggest that a combination of nonsurgical factors may influence the risk of local recurrence after curettage and bone-grafting of giant cell tumors of bone.
the most important factors associated with local control in GCTs are tumor size, surgical margin status, and histological subtype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an increased risk of recurrence in giant cell tumor patients who have undergone surgery for the primary lesion.

the use of a combination of 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) and indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence guidance in the surgical resection of gliomas is a promising technique for improving the extent of resection (EOR) and the postoperative survival of patients.
